source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 400 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 400 was established by Ordinance No. 22096, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 22, 1994. Ordinance No. 22096 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Ordinance No. 22096 was amended by Ordinance No. 24420, passed by the Dallas City Council on October 11, 2000. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 22096; 24420; 25850)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 400 is established on property generally located at the southwest and northwest corners of Merrell Road and Midway Road. The size of PD 400 is approximately 42.003 acres. (Ord. Nos. 22096; 25850; 32152)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.
(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article,

(1) AMPLIFIED SOUND means announcements, music, or other noise projected through stadium field sound speakers.

(2) ATHLETIC ACTIVITIES means athletic practices, scrimmages, and physical education classes limited to students of the private school located on the Property.

(3) ATHLETIC FIELD means the athletic fields located north of Merrell Road as shown on the development plan.

(4) AUTHORIZED ATHLETIC EVENT means an athletic game or school-sponsored athletic event published on the official website of the private school located on the Property.

(5) EAGLE WAY OUTDOOR LEARNING SPACE means an area for outdoor curricular activities or school event use as shown on the development plan.

(6) LOWER SCHOOL means beginner through fourth grade.

(7) MIDDLE SCHOOL means fifth grade through eighth grade.

(8) MONTWOOD LINE means a line designated on the development plan that limits development located to the south of the line in an area within 190 feet of the southern Property line.

(9) OUTDOOR CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES means any activity relating to the private school student educational experience and part of the routine school day or summer camp day limited use taking place in the Eagle Way Outdoor Learning Space.

(10) OVERFLOW PARKING means off-street parking for any event that is published on the official website of the private school located on the Property that is not a part of the routine school day and is limited to use for a maximum of 12 days per calendar year.

(11) ROUTINE SCHOOL DAY means scheduled school days, Monday through Friday, during Fall and Spring semester that include regular private school operations and educational classes.

(12) SCHOOL EVENT USE means use of the Eagle Way Outdoor Learning Space involving activities that are not part of the routine school day and are published on the official website of the private school located on the Property.

(13) SECURITY LIGHTING means outdoor lighting that provides a level of illumination to clearly identify persons or objects and creates a psychological deterrent to criminal activity in the area being protected. This use of lighting must not produce glare or direct illumination across a property line of an intensity that creates a nuisance or detracts from the use of adjacent property. Security lighting must be hooded and shielded except for bollard lighting.

(14) STADIUM FIELD means the athletic field at Jones Family Stadium as shown on the development plan.

(15) SUMMER CAMP DAY means scheduled school activity days, Monday through Friday in between spring and fall semester that include outdoor curricular use activities in the Eagle Way Outdoor Learning Space limited to student-maintained gardens.

(16) UPPER SCHOOL means ninth grade through 12th grade.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850; 32152)

SEC. 51P-400.103.1. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 400A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit 400B: south and southwest landscape buffer.

(3) Exhibit 400C: traffic management plan.

(4) Exhibit 400D: property description. (Ord. 32152)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 400A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) Future phases are not required to be developed in numerical sequence. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850; 32152)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the R-16(A) Single Family District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the R-16(A) Single Family District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the in the R-16(A) Single Family District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the R-16(A) Single Family District is subject to DIR in this district, etc.

(b) The following uses are permitted by right:

-- Private school. -- Tower/antenna for cellular communication. [Limited to no more than two cellular antennas mounted to stadium field light poles with cellular equipment as shown on the development plan.]

(c) The following use is permitted by SUP only:

-- School event use. [Food trucks and generators are allowed in conjunction with this use as set out in the SUP conditions.] (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850; 32152)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.106. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A- 4.217. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A- 4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the R- 16(A) Single Family District apply.

(b) Setbacks.

(1) Front yard. Minimum front along Merrell Road and Midway Road is 35 feet as shown on the development plan.

(2) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yard is 20 feet as shown on the development plan.

(3) Encroachments. Encroachments, fencing, stadium field light poles with or without mounted cellular equipment, and guard houses are permitted within the required setbacks as shown on the development plan.

(c) Floor area. Maximum floor area for each phase to be developed is shown on the development plan.

(d) Height.

(1) Maximum structure height is 48 feet, except as otherwise required by these conditions.

(2) Maximum structure height for Phases III, VI, and XIII is 35 feet.

(3) Maximum structure height for Phase X is 70 feet for the eastern 35 percent of the structure, and 48 feet for the remaining portion of the structure, as shown on the development plan.

(4) Maximum structure height for Phase XII is 30 feet.

(5) Spires and flagpoles may not exceed 70 feet, measured from grade to the highest point of the structure.

(6) Stadium field lighting poles may not exceed 60 feet in height with up to 12 additional feet in height for mounted cellular communication equipment.

(7) Parking lot light fixtures within 190 feet of the southern Property line south of the Montwood line may not exceed 12 feet in height.

(8) Maximum structure height for guardhouses is 12 feet.

(9) Residential proximity slope as defined in Section 51A-4.412 applies to all structures within the Property except for stadium field lighting poles with mounted cellular communication equipment.

(10) Projections are not permitted above the maximum structure height except for mounted cellular communication equipment on stadium field light poles.

(e) Lot coverage.

(1) Maximum lot coverage is 30 percent for nonresidential structures.

(2) For purposes of calculating lot coverage, the Property is considered one lot.

(f) Stories.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum number of stories above grade is three.

(2) Maximum number of stories above grade for Phase XIII is two. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850; 32152)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A- 4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Private school.

(1) Required parking. Off-street parking and loading must be provided as shown on the development plan. For a private school use, off-street parking is required as follows:

(A) Two spaces per lower school classroom.

(B) Three and one-half spaces per middle school classroom.

(C) Ten and one-half spaces per upper school classroom.

(D) No required parking for a school event use.

For purposes of calculating required off-street parking, the Property is considered one lot.

(2) Required loading.

(A) Off-street loading must be provided in accordance with Section 51A-

4.204(17).

(B) No required loading for a school event use.

(3) Phase XIII.

(A) Except as provided in this subsection, prior to and during construction of Phase XIII, a minimum of 430 off-street parking spaces must be provided on the Property.

(B) The loading and unloading zone may not be located within 105 feet of the south or west Property line and must have vehicular access from Eagle Family Way East only.

(4) Overflow parking.

(A) Overflow parking must be provided as shown on the development plan and must consist of grasscrete, enviro-crete, or a similar material as permitted in Section 51A-4.301(d)(4)(C), “Off-Street Parking Regulations.”

(B) Overflow parking may be used for a maximum of 12 days per calendar year and may not be used for any other purpose.

(C) Except during designated days utilizing overflow parking in Subparagraph
(B), ingress to and egress from overflow parking must be restricted from vehicular use by removeable bollards or similar device.

(5) Parking and idling restrictions.

(A) No bus parking or idling is allowed on Eagle Family Way South, west of Phase XIII, Eagle Family Way West, or on drive aisles or parking lots south of the Montwood line.

(B) No vehicle parking is allowed on Eagle Family Way South, west of Phase XIII, Eagle Family Way West, or on drive aisles south of the Montwood line except for vehicle queuing for carpool. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850; 32152)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.109. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850)

sections.title: Lighting And Noise
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.110. LIGHTING AND NOISE.

(a) Athletic field lighting. Athletic field lighting is not permitted except for bollard lighting for safety purposes that may not exceed 48 inches in height. Bollard lighting must be hooded and shielded, and light must be directed vertically downward and away from adjacent properties and stadium field lighting.

(b) Stadium field lighting.

(1) Stadium field lighting is permitted as shown on the development plan.

(2) Lighting may not produce glare or direct illumination across a Property line of an intensity that creates a nuisance or detracts from the use of adjacent properties.

(3) Except as provided in Paragraph (4), after May 1, 2022, stadium field lighting may only be used as follows:

(A) Monday through Wednesday:

(i) Between 6:45 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. in conjunction with athletic activities.

(ii) Between 6:45 a.m. and 8:30 p.m. in conjunction with authorized athletic events and events other than authorized athletic events, except that stadium field lighting may extend to 9:00 p.m. for a maximum of eight times per year.

(iii) During inclement weather, visiting athletic team or game officials travel delay, or overtime games, stadium field lighting for authorized athletic events may extend as late as:

(aa) 9:30 p.m. for a maximum of eight authorized athletic events per year; and

(bb) 9:00 p.m. all other times.

(B) Thursday through Friday:

(i) Between 6:45 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. in conjunction with athletic activities.

(ii) Between 6:45 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. in conjunction with authorized athletic events and events other than authorized athletic events.

(iii) During inclement weather, visiting athletic team or game officials travel delay, or overtime games, stadium field lighting for authorized athletic events may extend as late as 11:00 p.m. as long as the authorized athletic event starts no earlier than 8:00 p.m.

(C) Saturday:

(i) Between 8:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m., except that the stadium field lighting for authorized athletic events may extend to 10:00 p.m. or 30 minutes following the conclusion of an authorized athletic event, whichever is later.

(ii) During inclement weather, visiting athletic team or game officials travel delay, or overtime games, stadium field use for authorized athletic events may extend as late as 10:30 p.m.

(4) In addition to the times in Paragraph (3), stadium field lighting may be used in the following circumstances:

(A) When required maintenance cannot be reasonably accommodated between 6:45 a.m. and 8:00 p.m., stadium field lighting is permitted during required maintenance until 10:00 p.m., except on Sundays.

(B) In the event of an emergency situation, stadium field lighting is permitted at any time.

(C) During extreme weather conditions when the heat index is more than 100 degrees Fahrenheit, stadium field lighting is permitted as early as 6:00 a.m.

(D) Stadium field lighting is prohibited in the month of July.

(E) During the first week in November and the first two weeks in February, stadium field lighting is permitted as early as 6:30 a.m., Monday through Friday.

(c) Outdoor curricular activities and school event use noise. Outdoor curricular activities and school event use may not create a noise that exceeds the decibel level limit on the bounding lot line for a residential zoning district of 56 dBA or that exceeds the background noise level by five dBA, whichever is greater.

(d) Stadium field noise.

(1) Before the completion of the 2022 spring semester and before the completion of the 2022 fall semester, the Property owner or operator must provide two noise studies completed during a spring 2022 lacrosse game and a fall 2022 football game to the building official, prepared by a registered engineer, measuring noise generated from the stadium field during an authorized athletic event on adjacent residentially zoned properties south and east of the stadium field. If the director determines that the submitted noise analysis results in levels of noise that exceeds the standards in Article VI or otherwise creates a nuisance, the director shall require the Property owner to submit an outline of proposed improvements to mitigate reported noise levels. If the Property owner fails to submit an outline of the required improvements within 30 days after the director’s request, the director shall notify the city plan commission. The director may request additional stadium field noise studies no more than once every three years.

(2) Amplified sound is prohibited during athletic activities.

(3) Amplified sound is prohibited during authorized athletic events or events other than authorized athletic events, Sunday through Wednesday, except for the athletic team senior night and athletic team playoff games.

(4) Stadium sound compression devices must be installed to limit and monitor amplified sound from stadium speakers.

(5) Noise-amplifying devices such as bullhorns, airhorns, and vuvuzelas are prohibited. Signage must be posted at all spectator entrances of the stadium field advising of the prohibition for noise- amplifying devices. Notwithstanding this prohibition, game officials and coaches may use whistles and air horns. Whistles and airhorns must not create a noise that exceeds the decibel level limit on the bounding lot line for a residential zoning district of 56 dBA or that exceeds the background noise level by five dBA, whichever is greater.

(6) The use of artificial crowd noises or noise makers through amplification is also prohibited.

(7) Pre-game music and halftime music is only allowed for varsity level authorized athletic events.

(e) Noise monitoring device. A noise monitoring device must be installed on the eight-foot-high wood privacy fence on the south Property line, 150 feet west of Midway Road, to monitor noise levels emanating from the Property. Recorded noise levels must be published on the official website of the private school located on the Property.

(f) Parking lot lighting standards for lighting installed after February 23, 2022.

(1) The light source must be hooded and shielded.

(2) In order to direct light downward and minimize the amount of light spillage into the night sky and onto adjacent properties, all lighting fixtures must be full cutoff fixtures.

(3) Fixtures must be mounted in such a manner that the cone of the light is contained on- site and does not cross any property line on the perimeter of the Property.

(4) Parking lot lighting fixtures may not exceed 12 feet in height.

(g) Building and guardhouse security lighting standards for lighting installed after February 23, 2022.

(1) Building mounted security light fixtures such as wall packs may not project above the roof line of the building and must be hooded and shielded.

(2) Guardhouse security light fixtures must not exceed seven feet in height, must be hooded and shielded, and light must be directed vertically downward and away from adjacent properties.

(3) Internal guardhouse lighting must be turned off overnight between 11:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. or when unmanned.

(h) Building lighting. Existing and future building lighting must be turned off between 11:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m., except for motion security lights. With Phase XIII, internal lighting must be turned off between 8:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.

(i) Overflow parking lot. On Eagle Family Way North, South, East, and West driveways, entrances, and adjacent walkways lighting may only be provided as bollard lighting for safety purposes that may not exceed 48 inches in height. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850; 32152)

SEC. 51P-400.110.1. ATHLETIC FIELD AND STADIUM FIELD USE AND HOURS OF OPERATION.

(a) Athletic field.

(1) The athletic field may only be used for authorized athletic events, athletic activities, and other school-sponsored events.

(2) Events other than authorized athletic events are permitted on the athletic field a maximum of four days per calendar year.

(b) Athletic field hours of operation. The athletic field may only be used:

(A) between 6:45 a.m. and 8:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

(B) between 8:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. on Saturday.

(C) between 12:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. on Sunday.

(c) Stadium field.

(1) The stadium field may only be used for authorized athletic events, athletic activities, and other school-sponsored events.

(2) Events other than authorized athletic events are permitted on the stadium field a maximum of four days per calendar year.

(d) Stadium field hours of operation after May 1, 2022.

(1) Monday through Wednesday.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, the stadium field may only be used:

(i) between 6:45 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. in conjunction with athletic activities.

(ii) between 6:45 a.m. and 8:30 p.m. in conjunction with authorized athletic events, and other school-sponsored events.

(B) When using the stadium field, authorized athletic events may not be scheduled to start later than 7:00 p.m. and may not be scheduled to end later than 8:30 p.m., except that authorized athletic events may be scheduled to end at 9:00 p.m. a maximum of eight times per year.

(C) During extreme weather conditions when the heat index is more than 100 degrees Fahrenheit, stadium field use is permitted as early as 6:00 a.m.

(D) During inclement weather, visiting athletic team or game officials travel delay, or overtime games, stadium field use for authorized athletic events may extend as late as:

(i) 9:30 p.m. for a maximum of eight authorized athletic events per year; and

(ii) 9:00 p.m. all other times.

(E) During the first week in November and the first two weeks in February, use of the stadium field is permitted as early as 6:30 a.m.

(2) Thursday through Friday.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, the stadium field may only be used:

(i) between 6:45 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. in conjunction with athletic activities.

(ii) between 6:45 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. in conjunction with authorized athletic events, and other school-sponsored events.

(B) During extreme weather conditions when the heat index is more than 100 degrees Fahrenheit, stadium field use is permitted as early as 6:00 a.m.

(C) During inclement weather, visiting athletic team or game officials travel delay, or overtime games, stadium field use for authorized athletic events may extend as late as 11:00 p.m. as long as the authorized athletic event starts no earlier than 8:00 p.m.

(E) During the first week in November and the first two weeks in February, use of the stadium field is permitted as early as 6:30 a.m.

(3) Saturday.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, the stadium field may only be used between 8:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m., except that authorized athletic events may extend to 10:00 p.m. or 30 minutes following the conclusion of an authorized athletic event, whichever is later.

(B) During inclement weather conditions when the heat index is more than 100 degrees Fahrenheit, visiting athletic team or game officials travel delay, or overtime games, stadium field use for authorized athletic events may extend as late as 10:30 p.m.

(4) Sunday. The stadium field may only be used between 12:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. (Ord. 32152)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(2) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(b) A landscape plan that complies with this section must be submitted to the building official before a building permit will be issued for a phase of development.

(1) Artificial lots may be designated with each new permit.

(2) A landscape plan [must be submitted to and approved by the building official before a building permit will be issued for construction of the North Lot parking area shown on the development plan. The landscape plan must show one tree having a caliper of at least three inches provided in the parking lot for each 4,000 square feet of parking lot area, or fraction thereof, with a minimum of four trees being provided.

(3) Landscaping for Phase A, Phase B, and within the Phase XIII building site must be provided in accordance with this subsection and as shown on the south and southwest landscape buffer (Exhibit 400B).

(4) Prior to the issuance of a building permit for the Eagle Family Way South driveway, south staff parking lots, or Phase XIII building site, landscaping must be installed for the Phase A landscape buffer as shown on the south and southwest landscape buffer, and as indicated herein.

(5) Landscaping must be installed for the Phase B landscape buffer in conjunction with construction of the south staff parking lot as shown on the south and southwest landscape buffer.

(6) Landscaping must be installed for the Phase XIII landscape buffer in conjunction with construction of the Phase XIII building site with a 10-foot landscape buffer with large evergreen screening shrubs with a minimum height of six feet on the southern and western sides of the building site as shown on the south and southwest landscape buffer.

(7) The Phase A landscape buffer must be installed prior to Phase B or Phase XIII, except that the Phase A and Phase B landscape buffers may be installed concurrently.

(8) The Property owner or operator shall provide a health assessment of trees within the south and southwest landscape buffer area to the building official every three years following completion of Phase A landscaping. The health assessment must be prepared by a certified arborist. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850; 32152)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.112. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) A maximum of five monument signs with a maximum effective area of 144 square feet each and a maximum height of six feet each may be provided in the locations shown on the development plan. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850; 32152)

SEC. 51P-400.112.1. FENCE, SCREENING, AND VISUAL OBSTRUCTION REGULATIONS.

(a) A solid board-on-board wood perimeter fence must be provided along the south line of the Property and along 290 linear feet of the west line of the Property as shown on the development plan.

(b) The minimum height for the solid wood perimeter fence is eight feet.

(c) In addition to the requirements for Phase A landscaping as shown on the south and southwest landscape buffer, a minimum combined total of 50 large evergreen shrubs with a minimum height of eight feet at installation and trees with a caliper between six inches and eight inches at installation must be provided along the solid wood perimeter fence in the Phase A landscape buffer to provide additional screening for the benefit of adjacent residential properties. (Ord. 32152)

SEC. 51P-400.112.2. EAGLE WAY OUTDOOR LEARNING SPACE.

(a) The following may not be located within the Eagle Way Outdoor Learning Space within 190 feet north of the southern Property line and south of the Montwood line:

(1) Permanent playground structures.

(2) Temporary playground structures, except in accordance with an approved specific use permit for school events.

(3) Authorized athletic events, including cheerleading.

(4) Athletic team games or practices.

(5) Live or DJ music, outside speakers, outdoor choir, amplified sound, or microphones, except in accordance with an approved specific use permit for school events.

(6) Portable restrooms.

(b) The Eagle Way Outdoor Learning Space may only be used for outdoor curricular uses and in accordance with an approved specific use permit for school events.

(c) Lighting south of the Montwood line may only be provided as bollard lighting for safety purposes which may not exceed 48 inches in height.

(d) During summer camp days, outdoor curricular activities are limited to the student-maintained gardens only.

(e) The Eagle Way Outdoor Learning Space may only be used for outdoor curricular activities during the following hours:

(1) On routine school days, between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

(2) On summer camp days, between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. (Ord. 32152)

SEC. 51P-400.112.3. MAXIMUM ENROLLMENT FOR A PRIVATE SCHOOL.

A private school may not exceed a maximum enrollment of 1,400 students with an average daily on- campus attendance of 1,320 students. (Ord. 32152)

SEC. 51P-400.112.4. ADDITIONAL STANDARDS FOR PHASE XIII.

(a) The south and west elevations of structures must provide:

(1) variations in facade color and texture at least every 20 feet;

(2) a roof pitch greater than 15 degrees; and

(3) translucent glass or other screening for windows located anywhere from the finished floor to six feet above the finished floor on the second story of southeast, south, and west facing facades that obscures views into neighboring properties.

(b) Floor area for a single building may not exceed 7,500 square feet. Combined floor area for two buildings may not exceed 15,000 square feet.

(c) Buildings may be connected by a porte cochere, covered walkways, or other similar covered and open-air structures.

(d) Roof mounted equipment must be screened from adjacent properties and may not project above the 35-foot maximum structure height.

(e) Indoor lighting must be turned off between 11:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m., except for motion security lights.

(f) Outdoor lighting, except for security lighting, must be turned off by 8:00 p.m. on school nights and 7:00 p.m. on all other nights.

(g) Outdoor lighting, including security lighting, must be hooded and shielded, and light must be directed vertically downward and away from adjacent properties.

(h) Outdoor lighting, including security lighting, may not exceed seven feet in height.

(i) Use of the property within the Phase XIII site must comply with the following hours and days restrictions:

(1) Use of Phase XIII is limited to Monday through Friday between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. or later in conjunction with any events other than authorized athletic events that are published on the official website of the private school located on the Property.

(2) Closed on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays, except that school staff may access the building in conjunction with school-sponsored events published on the official website of the private school located on the Property and for cleaning and maintenance.

(j) Outdoor storage must be screened from view of adjoining residential property.

(k) Dumpsters may not be located within 150 feet of the south or west Property lines. Dumpsters must be screened from view of adjoining residential properties. Dumpster pickup is only allowed from Eagle Family Way East.

(l) A loading and unloading zone may not be located within 105 feet of the south or west Property line and must have vehicular accessibility from Eagle Family Way East only.

(m) No vehicular ingress and egress is permitted to the Phase XIII building site from Eagle Family Way South or West. (Ord. 32152)

sections.title: Traffic Management Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.113. TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN.

(a) In general. Operation of a private school must comply with the traffic management plan (Exhibit 400C).

(b) Queuing. Except as provided in the approved traffic management plan, queuing is only permitted inside the Property. Student drop-off and pick-up are not permitted within city rights-of-way.

(c) Traffic study.

(1) The Property owner or operator shall prepare a traffic study evaluating the sufficiency of the traffic management plan. The initial traffic study must be submitted to the director within 365 days after completion of the south entrance and south drive aisles as shown on the development plan. After the initial traffic study, the Property owner or operator shall submit updates of the traffic study to the director by March 1 of each odd-numbered year.

(2) The traffic study must be in writing, performed by a licensed engineer, based on a minimum of four samples taken on different school days at different drop-off and pick-up times over a two- week period, and must contain an analysis of the following:

(A) ingress and egress points;

(B) queue lengths;

(C) number and location of personnel assisting with loading and unloading of students;

(D) drop-off and pick-up locations;

(E) drop-off and pick-up hours for each grade level;

(F) hours for each grade level;

(G) circulation;

(H) total number of motor vehicles generated by school traffic during peak hours; and

(I) a school campaign that sets a specific goal to reduce the total number of vehicles participating in drop-off and pick-up operations. The traffic study must list the locations of signs displayed around the school that promote the campaign and list what incentives are available for student and family participation. The traffic study must include metrics to achieve a reduction in vehicular traffic by encouraging carpooling, walking, biking, and other practices.

(3) Within 30 days after submission of a traffic study, the director shall determine if the current traffic management plan is sufficient.

(A) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan is sufficient, the director shall notify the applicant in writing.

(B) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan results in traffic hazards or traffic congestion, the director shall require the Property owner to submit an amended traffic management plan. If the Property owner fails to submit an amended traffic management plan within 30 days, the director shall notify the city plan commission.

(4) Upon submission to the director, the traffic study and any subsequent updates must be published on the official website of the private school located on the Property.

(c) Amendment process.

(1) A traffic management plan may be amended using the minor plan amendment fee and public hearing process in Section 51A-1.105(k)(3).

(2) In order to amend a traffic management plan, the Property owner or operator must provide data showing the number of students who live within walking distance of the school, how many students actually walk to school, and how many students use public transportation.

(3) The city plan commission shall authorize changes in a traffic management plan if the proposed amendments improve queuing or traffic circulation; eliminate traffic hazards; or decrease traffic congestion. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850; 32152)

SEC. 51P-400.113.1. TRAFFIC REDUCTION AND CIRCULATION.

(a) Traffic reduction management must be continually pursued and carpooling and ride sharing must be promoted.

(b) Upon completion of Eagle Family Way North, Eagle Family Way South, and the south staff parking lots as shown on the development plan, student pickup and drop-off for the lower school must use the Midway Road entrance and student pickup and drop-off for the middle school and upper school must use the Merrell Road entrance.

(c) Upon completion of Eagle Family Way North, Eagle Family Way South, and the south staff parking lots as shown on the development plan, the Property owner or operator shall direct delivery vehicles, service vehicles, and buses to the Merrell Road entrance as the primary means of ingress and egress to the Property. Delivery vehicles, service vehicles, and buses must not use Eagle Family Way West or South, south of Phase XIII, at any time.

(d) Parking lot gates must be open and allow free-flow of vehicles into the Property one hour prior to the start time of authorized athletic events. (Ord. 32152)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) South of the Montwood line, the only permitted development includes paved and overflow parking, drive aisles, guard houses, monument signage, the Eagle Way Outdoor Learning Space, landscaping, and Phase XIII maintenance and administration support buildings limited to a maximum of 15,000 square feet, as shown on the development plan.

(b) Upon application for a minor amendment, specific use permit, or zoning change, the Property owner or operator shall notify property owners within 500 feet of the Property 30 days prior to submitting the application through the designated representative of the Walnut Hill Homeowners Association (WHHA) that is registered on the “homeowner association early notification list” maintained by the department of planning and urban design of the city.

(c) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(d) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 24420; 25850; 32152)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-400.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22096; 25850; 32152)
